message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** of how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and boots from Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
The example uses the **REST API** (via `curl`) because that is what you normally mean by “API call.”  
I also include a quick `gcloud` command‑line equivalent so you can verify the result or use it in a script.

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** and the **GPU API** (`compute.googleapis.com`) are enabled.  
> * You have a service account key (JSON) or an OAuth 2.0 access token that has the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or higher).  
> * You have the `gcloud` CLI installed if you want to use the command‑line alternative.  

---

## 1. REST API (curl)

```bash
# Variables – replace these with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"       # RTX A6000
DISK_SIZE_GB=100              # boot disk size
DISK_TYPE="pd-standard"       # persistent disk type
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"

# Get an OAuth 2.0 access token (if you have gcloud installed)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# Build the JSON body
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_BODY <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/$MACHINE_TYPE",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/$IMAGE_PROJECT/global/images/family/$IMAGE_FAMILY",
        "diskSizeGb": $DISK_SIZE_GB,
        "diskType": "zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/$DISK_TYPE"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": $GPU_COUNT,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/$GPU_TYPE"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# Make the API call
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_BODY"
```

### What the JSON does

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name |
| `machineType` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image, size, type |
| `networkInterfaces[0]` | Default VPC + external IP |
| `guestAccelerators[0]` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `serviceAccounts[0]` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Optional startup script that installs the NVIDIA driver |

> **Note**: The NVIDIA driver version (`535` in the script) may change. Check the [official NVIDIA driver list](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus/install-drivers-gpu) for the latest supported driver for RTX A6000.

---

## 2. Equivalent `gcloud` command

If you prefer to use the `gcloud` CLI, the same instance can be created with:

```bash
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size="$DISK_SIZE_GB"GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
  --metadata=startup-script='#!/bin/bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535' \
  --scopes=cloud-platform
```

This command does exactly what the REST call does, but it’s often easier to read and debug.

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After the instance is created, you can verify the GPU attachment:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --format="json(guestAccelerators)"
```

You should see an entry like:

```json
"guestAccelerators": [
  {
    "acceleratorCount": 1,
    "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"
  }
]
```

---

## 4. Common pitfalls & tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Quota exceeded** | Request a GPU quota increase in the Cloud Console. |
| **GPU not available in zone** | Use a zone that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`). |
| **Driver not installed** | Ensure the startup script runs after the instance boots. |
| **Billing disabled** | Instances with GPUs require billing to be enabled. |
| **Access token expired** | Refresh the token (`gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`) or use a service account key. |

---

### TL;DR

- **REST API**: `curl` POST to `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/.../zones/.../instances` with a JSON body that includes `guestAccelerators` for `nvidia-a6000`.  
- **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1`.  

Both approaches will give you an Ubuntu 20.04 LTS VM with an RTX A6000 GPU ready for your workloads. Happy computing!
